utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Mr. Court Deputy, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I believe that you have already reviewed your statement yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I make a comment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stated yesterday that the document signed by Mr. Borovcanin, I said that I wasn't sure whether it was his signature or not. I think that that is not his signature, and if I may suggest for that to be submitted to a handwriting expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you. I think in the redirect, the Prosecution will ask some questions in this aspect. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before I begin the questioning, good morning, Mr. Jevic. How are you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, I am fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before I ask the questions that I prepared, might I ask how is it that you came up with this idea this morning that the signature was not Mr. Borovcanin's? What was it that caused you to come up with this revelation?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't sure about that signature and I said so yesterday and then thinking about it and analysing that, the fact that Mr. Borovcanin is my superior, and if we're talking truthfully and correctly, the report where his signature is placed, that there's been something perhaps erased or changed there and that is what made me come to this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, before we go into your statement as we left off yesterday, I want to pick up first and discuss the order that was presented to you, and I believe has been marked for identification purposes as P157. And if we could give it to the gentleman. Yesterday you were shown this order. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And yesterday you were asked by the Prosecution what was your understanding of this order. What did you actually do pursuant to the order. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it it was based on this order that you began the mobilisation process, is that correct, in order to go to Bratunac and then on to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says in my statement, and I explained here in the courtroom yesterday, that Mr. Borovcanin came to me, to the Jahorina camp with a written order and an oral order. And that is how I understood it and that is how I responded to these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So in other words that order which is 157 for identification purposes, P157, that order, even though you were copied with it, you were served a copy of it, that was not the order that you acted upon, rather from that order your supervisor Borovcanin prepared an order for you, a specific order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's a multi-part question again. And it's also I believe a misstatement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll break it down but it's not a misstatement of the evidence and if the Prosecutor is going to be making these comments, I would ask Your Honour that he point specifically how I am mischaracterising the evidence. I understand he wishes to protect his witness, but if he's going to make comments like these on the record, he should substantiate them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, try to ask a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: After you got a copy of this order, sir, it's your testimony that Mr. Borovcanin came to you with another order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in my statement that Mr. Borovcanin came to the Jahorina camp to see me and said we have an order to go to Bratunac and that we should get ready. So I carried out only the orders of my superiors. I got the unit ready and went to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Jevic, did Mr. Borovcanin tell you what units you should get ready, how many men, what equipment to take, or did he just say we're going off to Bratunac? What exactly did Mr. Borovcanin tell you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin said that he had an order that a company was to go to Bratunac. The only equipment that we had at the time was what we could take with us. That was all we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was the same order that you received a copy of. Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And based on that order, Mr. Borovcanin then approached you and told you what your responsibilities would be with respect to the mission towards Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me to go to Bratunac for an assignment and that there we would receive a direct order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did he tell you how many men to take with you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that a company was supposed to go, namely, that that is what it says in the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it it was your responsibility to form that company?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my responsibility to prepare the company so that it could travel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then you travelled along with company, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when Mr. Borovcanin came to you, did he tell you that you, MUP, that is, were subordinated or resubordinated to the VRS, and in particular to General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't say that then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so based on that order, you went to Bratunac on the 11th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the first thing that you did is you found accommodations for you and your men outside of Bratunac in some village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did you locate those accommodations or were they located for you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think that our accommodations were already prepared for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: By whom? Was it MUP? Was it General Mladic, General Krstic, General Zivanovic? Who was it who prepared those accommodations for you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir. When I came to Bratunac, I reported to Mr. Borovcanin and I was told to go to find our accommodation at the school in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Sir, was it Mr. Borovcanin that directed you to your accommodations?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, yesterday you were asked some questions about the rules. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I understand it that it was your testimony that -- and I quote here, and I'm quoting from page 27. It begins with line 6 -- or line 5. The question was: "Were these rules related to who was in command when the special police are working with the army?" Do you recall being -- sir.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I'm questioning you -- I'm not talking about your statement. I'm reading from your -- I'm reading from your testimony, the transcript that we have from yesterday, okay. So it won't be in the statement. Okay?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. The Prosecutor -- sir, it's not in that statement, so you might as well put it down. We'll get to that statement, trust me. We will get to it. Now, according to the official transcript prepared by the Tribunal, yesterday you were asked a question by the Prosecutor, Mr. McCloskey who's sitting there. And the question was: "Were these rules related to who was in command when the special police are working with the army?" And the answer was, the answer that you gave: "The rules that were applied, or rather, used at the time in the area had been taken over from the former Yugoslavia where if there was an imminent threat of war or a state of war, the police were resubordinated to the military, to the army, and placed at the disposal of the army to use them as they saw fit." Do you recall making that statement, sir, yesterday on the record under oath?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly, as far as I know, that is what the rules state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And -- well I'm most particular in making sure that it's your understanding of the rules, given your level of experience as an inspector, as an assistant commander, as an instructor, that once resubordinated, MUP is placed at the disposal of the army to use them as they saw fit. In other words, that the army can use MUP as they see fit. Is that your understanding of the rules and the law?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the rules say in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, might I ask, sir, given that you are an instructor, a trainer, that you've had an opportunity to review the rules. Let me ask the question again. As an instructor, have you consulted or do you consult the rules?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, vague. There's quite a bit of rules. If we could get more specific, it might be more helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, do you have the rules at your hands?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I do have the rules. I just want to get to the general, because the Prosecutor yesterday used the word "rules". So I'm using the same vague terminology that the Prosecutor used for which this particular witness yesterday had no problem coming up with an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you had better directly show the rules to this witness. That will be easier for everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I don't want to argue with the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, before coming here today, did you have a chance to read the law on defence?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And before coming here, did you have an opportunity to read the law on the implementation of the law on internal affairs during imminent threat of war or a state of war?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you familiar with those laws?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not read them myself, but I was informed about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Might I conclude before I go to the rules that you don't use these rules or these laws in your everyday training?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's just get to them. If I could show you what has been marked for identification purposes as D60/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the record, I've only copied the relevant portion, which is only one article, but we do intend to copy the entire law, but I'm told that it was somewhat efficient this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if you could look, sir -- and I should note that for the record there is a number, a Prosecution number on top, it's 00848628 of the first page. Do you see this, sir? Do you see the document and does it not appear to be from the Official Gazette of the RS?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me where this number is, 00 ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Just look at the title, sir. Look at the title that is in Cyrillic. Does it not say Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And does it not say that this is a copy or is this not the copy of the law on defence in the Official Gazette of the RS?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it states here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And the date -- do you see a date there? Does it have a date by any chance?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says June 1st, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could go to Article 7, sir. Article 7, which would be on the second page, and you go to subparagraph number 6, right. So I'm going to read the top portion. It says: "As part of organising preparation for defence, the president of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina shall," and then I go to 6. And it states "define the organisation of the size of the police force, issue orders for the deployment of the police in time of war, the imminent threat of war, and during a state of war of emergency to protect the rights and duties of the republic and its citizens stipulated in its constitution and laws." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that based on this article here, that it is the -- the MUP assets are under the direction or directed by the president of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot interpret that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now let's -- let me show you what has been marked for identification purposes as D61/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the record, the Prosecution number begins with 00860442.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could just look it over, flip through the pages, just so you -- and look at the titles. Have you done that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen the titles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the first page, we see that there is a decree, a decree on the promulgation on the law, of the implementation of the law on internal affairs during an imminent threat of war or a state of war. I understand that may not -- you may not have that, but for the record that's on the first page in the English version. Okay. The first page that you have, sir, should have the law of the implementation on the law of internal affairs. Do you see that? Do you see the title, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And does the title not read: "Law on the implementation on the law of internal affairs during an imminent threat of war or state of war"?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if you could look at article 1, article 1, does it not state, sir, that this law regulates the procedure to be adopted by the Ministry of Interior during an imminent threat of war or state of war. Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you as part -- you being the special police force, were part of the Ministry of Interior, were you not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So it would appear, would it not, sir, that this law would apply to your unit, you yourself, and your commander, Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as well as Mr. Kovac, who was, I believe, the deputy minister at the time. Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think he was the deputy minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It's irrelevant what Mr. Karnavas believes. This constant injection of his personal opinions is just not relevant and not proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, first I think you have to concentrate on this law and later on you may ask some relevant questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. But just for the record, we do have a document that was introduced by the Prosecution as P175, and the Prosecutor does know exactly what Mr. Kovac's position was. So I believe the Prosecution is doing nothing but obstructing at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could go to article 4, sir. If you could look at article 4.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, it states here in the first paragraph: "The ministry shall be considered a part of the armed forces of the Republika Srpska and its forces shall be under the command of the President of the Republika Srpska as the commander-in-chief." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So in other words, you are serving under the command of Karadzic at the time, who was the President of the RS?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic was the President of Republika Srpska at that point, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So under article 4, it would appear, would it not, that you are under, MUP that is, in general, your unit as well, are under the command of the President of the RS?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know who my commander was, and the unit was commanded by the minister of internal affairs. As far as any further chain of command is concerned, I can't comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, if we could move to article 12. Does it not state, sir, that "distinct from special purpose police units, the Ministry of Interior shall establish special police units to carry out combat tasks."

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were in charge of a special police unit, were you not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, what were you? Were you a regular traffic police?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not an officer of the special police at that time, not the officer in charge. I was maybe number five in the pecking order as far as the officers of the special police were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you were serving in the special police. Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the special police, and this is something I've never tried to deny.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm not saying that you denied it, but that special police unit was established by the Ministry of Interior, right, if the law was followed under article 12?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we get to article 13. And if you just look at the second -- we can read the whole thing, it's a short article. "Police units shall participate in combat operations pursuant to an order issued by the commander-in-chief of the armed forces and the minister of interior." Now, when it talks about the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, we're talking about Karadzic, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the Ministry of Interior, well we know that's high up the chain of command from where you were serving, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Far above me, far above me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Then the next paragraph says: "The minister of interior shall give orders to the police units through the ministry police forces command staff." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now we get to article 14. Let's read along. "Police units assigned to combat operation by an order of the commander-in-chief of the armed forces shall be resubordinated to the commander of the unit in whose zone of responsibility they are performing combat tasks." Clear enough, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then we'll read the whole article. "Police units shall be under the direct command of a commander who is a member of the Ministry of Interior. During the time they are resubordinated to the Army of Republika Srpska, they shall retain their organisation and may not be split up or separated." Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, from this, just as an aside, this little paragraph basically says, would you not agree with me, that the army cannot do whatever it wishes with MUP when they are resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand your comments, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you said in your statement or in your testimony yesterday that: "When they are subordinated, they are placed at the disposal of the army to use them as they saw fit." So the army, however they see fit, can use MUP. That was your testimony yesterday on page 27, and I just read from lines 10 to 12.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that we were resubordinated to the army as far as the chain of command is concerned. It was in that sense that orders were carried out that were given by the army. I meant nothing, aside from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's read on. The third paragraph in article 14 says: "Police units resubordinated to the Army of Republika Srpska in a certain zone shall be used only for combat operations established in advance by the commander-in-chief or the minister of interior." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, would you not -- this seems to indicate that in advance of the combat operation, the commander-in-chief or the minister of interior must establish exactly what it is that MUP is supposed to be doing. Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you're an educated man, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's not what it says, first of all. It doesn't say "exactly".

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll reread it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And now we're getting into this demeaning questioning which, it just doesn't take us anywhere. I've not found witnesses to be able to respond to this kind of demeaning question, no matter who they are or what they previously testified to. I think it demeans the process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey opened the door by asking him to comment on the rules. Yesterday I indicated for them to present the rules. He chose not to. I was told yesterday that I have free access to go into this area. I locked the witness into indicating that he was educated. He's an instructor. He indicated, in fact, that he felt demeaned because he was in charge of people who had fled and were not serving and that the implication being that obviously he should have been at a higher position. He had an opinion yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, let me ask the witness a question. Witness, you said that you can't answer the question. Can you tell us why.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a different level from mine, the level required to answer this kind of question. I don't know about this level of assignment. I can't offer any comments on that. Please accept my apologies, Mr. Presiding Judge. I did require protective measures for my testimony at one point, the reason was my respect for this institution. The reason was my respect for the law. Over the last ten years, my family and I had certain problems, but that doesn't matter because those are my personal problems. However, then I decided, Mr. President, to testify in public, in open session, because I had nothing to hide. But please understand this: I cannot be made to answer for the responsibilities of some other people that were far above my station in terms of the chain of command. I have the education that I have. I did what I did. I am not ashamed of what I did. I am here today to answer fair questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe the problem is that this question is very complicated, Mr. Karnavas. And because of the difference and because of the different training, this question may trigger the different understandings than the interpretations. Mr. Karnavas, could you split your question and use the simplest language to come across your ideas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Based on your response to the President's question, sir, am I to understand that what we're discussing here right now, the law, is above your level of knowledge and expertise?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I am no expert in legal matters. I can't interpret laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So is the answer yes to my question?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll repeat the question. Based on your answers that you gave to the President's inquiry, are we to understand that you are not competent and lack the knowledge in commenting on the law and the rules with respect to subordination and resubordination and the use of MUP by the army?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not competent to interpret these laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So if you're not competent today, I take it you weren't competent yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I object to that question, Your Honour. I was clearly asking what his understanding of a simple rule was. He gave us his understanding. It's actually pretty close to this rule and he said that was his rough understanding. This is out of -- it's out of line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I don't think he's out of the line, but this is true that yesterday you asked a very simple question and it seemed to me the witness answered this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll move on to the next area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, based on -- I want to show you what has been marked for identification as D62.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record, this, too, has a Prosecution number on it. 00888578.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could just look at that, sir, and we're going to focus on the first two paragraphs, paragraph number one and paragraph number two. If you could just look at it first.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if you look at the last page, the second page. Now, it seems from the last page that this is an order by the supreme commander of the armed forces of Republika Srpska, Dr. Radovan Karadzic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it appears to be, an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could look at paragraph number 1. Does it not state that: "The main staff of the army shall henceforth define more precisely and concretely their request for engagement and employment of MUP units in combat in accordance with the provisions of article 14 of the law and application of the law on interior affairs during imminent threat of war and state of war, item 4 of the Official Gazette, Republika Srpska, special edition number 1." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And article 14, as you recall, is the one we just went through. Do you recall that? There's no need to look at the Prosecutor. You can just answer the question.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Paragraph 2, "When MUP units are engaged in combat as part of the VRS troops, the Republika Srpska MUP shall precisely specify the responsibilities of the commanding officers and commanders when they are resubordinated to the commander of the VRS unit in whose area of responsibility they are carrying out their combat tasks, pursuant to provisions of article 14 of the aforementioned law, with its order to engage and subordinate for execution of the given assignment as per place and time of the engagement on which to establish necessary coordination with the GS VRS/Army of Republika Srpska." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, are you able to understand these two paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What exactly the supreme commanders --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do not -- these two paragraphs actually are directing the VRS to be very specific when engaging -- when MUP are being resubordinated to them and to make sure that they strictly adhere to article 14 of the law on the implementation, the one that we just read?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the rules say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's what the rules say and this is what the supreme commander is ordering, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, if we could go to plaintiff's exhibit -- I mean prosecution exhibit P157, the Kovac order of July 10, 1995. And if you look at the last paragraph, which is paragraph number 5.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'll read it for the record and then we'll discuss it. "On arrival at the destination, the unit commander shall contact General Krstic, the corps chief of staff." Does it state that in Srpski?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I'm particularly interested in the word "contact." From this word, does it say anything about resubordination?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't comment on that. This is a matter of terminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. When you say it's a matter of terminology, are you suggesting that in Srpski, and in particular the way that word is used in the military or MUP context, it has a different meaning?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm no expert in linguistic interpretation, therefore you can hardly expect me to interpret this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so from your answer, I take it you can hardly interpret that this means that MUP is resubordinated to the VRS, can you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, the MUP was resubordinated to the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. My question --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. These statements are unnecessary. They are out of line. They're not questions. It's just argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think this is a very important issue and the Defence counsel has the right to make it very clear, at least to us. Maybe, Mr. Karnavas, you could change the form of your question somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From reading paragraph 5, are you suggesting here today, sir, that "contact," the word "contact," means resubordination?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding was that he should get in touch in order to receive assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, does it say anywhere here on paragraph 5, "contact General Krstic or the corps chief of staff so you can get assignments, since you are now resubordinated to the VRS." Does it say anything of that sort?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That is argumentative, Your Honour. We can clearly see it doesn't say that. That's pure argumentative. It's an important issue, I agree. But this does not help us get to the bottom of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Jevic, when Mr. Borovcanin, your supervisor, your boss, met with General Krstic, were you present?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see anything in writing generated as a result of the meeting, the contact, between your boss, Borovcanin, and General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you have no idea of what was said at that time, do you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to show you what has been marked for identification purposes, again another Prosecution document. It's P109.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I have -- perhaps we could put this on the ELMO as well. It might be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could look --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have a copy in B/C/S here for the gentleman. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did the Prosecution have a chance to share with you this document that they have in their possession?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If you flip to the second page, the last -- well, if you look at the bottom of the page, there's a signature there, is there not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who is Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic was the chief of the public security centre in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And is he not MUP like you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So he, too, is under the Ministry of Interior, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could look at the very first paragraph, not the ones that are numbered, but the very top, starting with the first line. "During the meeting held this morning with General Mladic, we were informed that the VRS/Army of Republika Srpska/ is resuming with the operation towards Zepa and is yielding all other tasks to MUP. These tasks being," and it lists the tasks. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the date on this, is it not 13 July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, it would appear that this is a letter or a memo. The Prosecution has titled it CJB document, and it's addressed to the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And from this document, he being a MUP just like you, would it not appear that the army is yielding, not ordering, certain tasks to be carried out by MUP?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this document, yes, indeed that's what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. All right. So the army is not ordering MUP. MUP is on its own to do these tasks?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Very well. Incidentally, now that you've read your statement, the statement that you gave to the Prosecution back in 18 October, 2002, you make no mention of this order by Mr. Kovac of 10 July, 1995, do you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I gave the statement before that year and I was not aware of this order, and that's why I could refer to it. I do believe, however, that I mentioned the deputy minister, Mr. Kovac's, order in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned that based on this order it was your understanding that you were subordinated?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly was subordinated to Mr. Borovcanin. That was according to the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Jevic, there is nothing in your statement with respect to this order, that is the Kovac order that was addressed to you back on 10 July, 1995. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did mention it in my order -- statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps during the break you can find it, because I have been unable to do so. Okay. Now I want to move on to another segment, something different, and it's with respect to Mr. Nikolic. You know Mr. Nikolic, do you not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, you knew him prior to July 11th, 1995, when you showed up in Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you think so or you know so? You either knew him or you didn't know.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, yesterday I just want to first discuss -- let me -- let's talk about -- I want to share with you what Mr. Nikolic had to say when questioned by Mr. McCloskey here in court, and I'm going to refer to the transcript. I have a copy for the ELMO. There are four pages and we're going to go page by page. So if I could have the indulgence of the usher to assist. I'm going to read now from page 1684, questioning examination done by Mr. McCloskey, witness Momir Nikolic, Monday 22 September, 2003, line 14. It says:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What did Colonel Jankovic say to you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Jankovic told me what my next assignment would be. He said on the 12th I should work in Potocari and coordinate the activities that were underway in Potocari itself and that I should give instructions and that I should coordinate the evacuation of the civilian population, of the women and the children, to coordinate work on the separation of the men and the temporary transfer and detention." Now, if we flip over to the next page which is 1685, we'll read from line 5 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If he's going to comment, which I imagine that's what he's doing, but if he's taking sections that are potentially out of context, the comment may come out of context. I have no objection to a comment on some key phrase, but I don't know how he's going to possibly answer -- are we going to read back half the testimony? I mean, that is an improper form of questioning. I mean if we can go one at a time and keep it specific, I have no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, in this situation, can you put your question to this witness first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I cannot, Your Honour. Because he answered his question yesterday and now what I'm attempting to do is give him an opportunity to hear what Nikolic had to say when questioned by the Prosecutor, not by Karnavas, but none other than the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you repeat your question yesterday and to see after refreshment of the memory of this witness overnight there's any changes. If not, you have the right to present your case to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. With all due respect, however, I believe I should be entitled to do my cross-examination the way I have organised it and not the way the Prosecution feels it should be organised. I apologise if they wish to know in advance what I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Karnavas, during the cross-examination it is very important to let us, the Judges, to understand your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's why I'm going from the general to the specific. That's why I took the time to do all of this and then I was going to point him to his particular, but I'll do it the reverse. I'll rework it, Your Honour, I'll be flexible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the aim is the same. The approach could be varied.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand. Very well, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at what you stated yesterday when you were being questioned by the Prosecutor himself. Now, at one point and I'm making a reference -- I'm referring you to page 38, and it's line 14, it states, and this is you, sir, "In conversation in Banja Luka, during the interview in Banja Luka in 2001 or 2000, I heard that Mr. Nikolic said that I was the one who coordinated the separation of the people in Potocari together with him, but I responsibly state that that is not so," and then you go on. That was the first reference. Now, on the second page, on another page, and now I'm referring to page 40. I'm going to go from page 40 on to 41. I'm starting with line 17. This was yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In July of 1995, did you know who Momir Nikolic was? Same question I asked you today.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Momir Nikolic from before. No equivocation. You say that you knew him. Then next question by Mr. McCloskey himself:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with Momir Nikolic on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see Momir Nikolic in Potocari on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you talked with me, I also said that I did not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know we have gone over things and I know it's repeating, so did you see Mr. Nikolic on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you're aware that Momir Nikolic has stated that he communicated with you regarding the transportation of Muslim citizens from Potocari on the 12th and 13th. What do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that I as a man honourably on the 12th and 13th did not -- did what I was ordered to do. And the statements by Momir Nikolic are not correct, and I think that has nothing to do with me. I either as a person or as a police officer would not permit myself to commit such acts. Mr. Nikolic didn't say that he committed any acts of abuse -- this is a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic didn't say that you committed any acts of abuse as I recall. He said that you were just organising the transportation of the Muslim prisoners in regard to what he -- in regard what he said about you. And then you go on, and this is on line 16, you state, "I simply directed the people. I turned around the trucks and the buses." That was your testimony, sir, yesterday. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall the testimony of yesterday, not in such a context. I think that perhaps I did not state that so decisively. I can confirm that on the 12th, I was in Potocari, that I did what I was ordered to do. And I said that I do not recall seeing Mr. Nikolic in Potocari. I, again, say that I do not remember. I was busy on my own tasks. At that point, I was working as a signalsman. I was turning the buses around. People -- during my questioning in Banja Luka, I was shown a tape of some men. Later I heard that Mr. Nikolic said that I was the one who took part in the separation of men and women. I responsibly state that the only things that I did was turning around the buses and the trucks, people were entering them, and then they were leaving on the road in the direction of Kladanj. I stand by my statement. I find that no additional comments are necessary. I'm very sorry that somebody is trying to represent this in some other way. I do not recall seeing Nikolic. So I simply cannot say that I remember doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So I take it now your testimony is that you did know, you did in fact know, Momir Nikolic prior to the 11th of July, 1995. Can we establish that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I knew him before that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I would like to refer to you what he has said on the record under oath, about being questioned by Mr. McCloskey, and then have your comment on this. And I'm reading from page 1685 of the official transcript. Monday the 22nd of September, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Colonel Jankovic refer you to any particular person to conduct these duties in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He, he told me that as for coordinating those duties that were part of the operation I should speak with Mr. Jevic who was a member of the special brigade of the MUP. Dusko Jevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know who Dusko Jevic was at the time?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Dusko Jevic personally. I know him from before the operation, but at that time I didn't know precisely what his role in Potocari was. I knew he was a member of the special brigade of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, but I didn't know what specifically his role was. And then further down on line 19,.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At that time did you know the hierarchy between Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Jevic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, roughly yes, I was aware of it. I knew Mr. Borovcanin was Mr. Jevic's superior. Now, Mr. Jevic, now that you have heard what Mr. Nikolic has said, do you still maintain that you had no contact with him on that particular day of the 12th and that he did not give you any orders or was not assisting you in coordinating the activities in which you were involved?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I do not remember. I cannot say decisively. I simply stated that I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So it's a possibility. Are you now suggesting that the possibility exists that Momir Nikolic was giving you orders on what you should be doing on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I do not recall seeing or communicating with Momir Nikolic. Any other comments would just be superfluous or any conclusions I could draw on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me go on and I'm reading from page 1690, 1690. I'll start with line 17, again being questioned by Mr. McCloskey himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you carry out the instructions that you had heard from Kosoric, Popovic, and Colonel Jankovic?" This is to Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did exactly what I had been ordered to do, exactly in the way in which I was issued instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what you did?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the first buses arrived or, rather, just before, I got in touch with Mr. Jevic. I told him how the evacuation should be conducted and what his role was in connection with the buses, organising those buses, and other issues related to the transport of the civilian population. Then I gave instructions to units who were separating the men from the rest, I gave them instructions to separate all military-aged men in Potocari, and I showed them the house in which these men were to be temporarily detained. After that, I said the men would be taken to other facilities that were assigned for the temporary detention. Now, Mr. Jevic, have you --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now that you have heard what Mr. Momir Nikolic has stated in this very same courtroom, do you still maintain that Momir Nikolic did not give you any orders or assignments?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that I do not remember and I stated that the order from Kovac was something that I received from my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me be a little more precise. What you've stated, and correct me if I'm wrong, is that you don't recall seeing Mr. Nikolic on that particular day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You don't recall having contact with Mr. Nikolic that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you're also saying today that you don't recall whether Mr. Nikolic actually ordered you or gave you instructions on that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that I do not recall seeing him or talking with Mr. Nikolic. The instructions from the Kovac order I received from my superior, Mr. Borovcanin, and I cannot say that I remember something if I do not remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe it -- I can continue or we can take a break, Your Honour. It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll break until 10 minutes to 11.00. --- Break taken at 10.18 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. For the record, I want to bring to everyone's attention, especially to Mr. Jevic's attention, that he did, in fact, in his statement indicate the order from Mr. Kovac who he believed at the time was the deputy minister and it is on page 14, line 6 to 10, page 10, line 25-26 and then to the next page in B/C/S. So you were correct, sir, and I do apologise. I also want to apologise this morning for being on the short end of my nerves. Something in the coffee, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we could get back to Potocari on 12th July, 1995. Based on your statement and based on your testimony, it appears that you were taking all of your instructions from your superior officer, Mr. Borovcanin. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received my orders from Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. As I recall, you and Mr. Borovcanin were in Potocari sometime at 9.00 in the morning, 9.30?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 9.00, 9.30, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at that point, he had given you some basic instructions as far as what you would be doing and what your men would be doing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period, Mr. Borovcanin had met with General Mladic near a house. They spoke. I'm not aware of what they talked about. Before that, instructions were issued that the evacuation would proceed the next day and that we would take part in that evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But that was on the -- we're talking about the 12th, the morning of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received the Kovac order already on the 11th, meaning that the agreement had been reached and that the next day Potocari would be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So when you went to Potocari, Mr. Borovcanin was there as well, was he not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And your company commanders were there as well, were they not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was that Mr. Djuric?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think he has an nickname Mane. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it he was tasked as well, was he not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he was under your command, was he not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so while you were in Potocari on the 12th, the orders were coming to you from Mr. Borovcanin and then you would direct your men, including your company commander, as far as what they would be doing during that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I take it that Mr. Nikolic, if he were -- if he were to give any instructions to you personally, since your commanding officer was there at the time, Mr. Borovcanin, would it not be under the proper military chain of command that he would go through Mr. Borovcanin and not to you directly?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's assume hypothetically speaking that Colonel Jankovic had given a particular task to Momir Nikolic. If you were receiving all of your orders from your commander, Mr. Borovcanin, and if Mr. Borovcanin was still in the area, as you've indicated, would Mr. Nikolic not have to go through Mr. Borovcanin to give you the orders?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. The witness said he didn't know. These gratuitous comments again. I hate to keep objecting, but it's improper for him to be making these gratuitous comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could someone from another unit give you an order directly in Potocari on the 12th if your commander, Mr. Borovcanin, was there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. From what other unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let's just say that Colonel Pandurevic was there from the Zvornik Brigade and he decided that he wanted to give Stalin an order and Mr. Borovcanin was there. Could Pandurevic give you an order directly or would he have to go through Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I do not object to hypothetical questions to this witness, but if they're going to be related to the facts, as this one was, Potocari, they need to be based on the facts, and this one was not. We don't have any facts that Mr. Pandurevic was around. It is not improper to give him a hypothetical, a general military-type hypothetical, but if he's going to bring it into the Potocari arena, it needs to be based on the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I ask, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, usually this kind of question is not allowed, but in this situation, the purpose of the Defence counsel is to know the commander chain, how does the order goes, so we allow Mr. Karnavas to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you remember the question that was asked of you, Mr. Jevic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's say an officer from another unit, not MUP, outside of MUP, wished to give you a direct order to do something, if Mr. Borovcanin, your commander, was there at the scene, would he not have to go through your commander to give the order and not to you directly?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, naturally, the order could only be passed on through Mr. Borovcanin. I must say that throughout the period, General Mladic was present, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And General Mladic was giving orders as well, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But now with respect to Mr. Nikolic, you can't compare Momir Nikolic, a reserve captain, and General Mladic, can you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we move on to the next section, on that particular day, on the 12th, was there a situation where you had taken a leave of absence of your duties while you were -- while you came across a Mercedes Benz bus that was worth approximately 2 million Deutschmarks? Do you recall that incident? Was it that day or the next day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure on which day that happened. The bus was handed over to Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you sure it was handed over and you didn't just take it to try to sell it in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, never in my life was I a thief, which you are obviously trying to insinuate. I never tried anything like that. My orders were for the bus to be handed over to Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was that an order that was given to you by your commander, Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if he would have told the Prosecutor somewhat differently, would you still maintain your position that you had received an order from Mr. Borovcanin to take this Mercedes Benz bus that was worth approximately 2 million Deutschmarks and go off to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My order from Mr. Borovcanin was to hand the bus over in the area of Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Let's move on to another area, and now I want to move ahead to the 16th of July. I believe it was your testimony yesterday that you indicated that you were advised or ordered to report to the Bratunac Brigade on the evening of the 16th to meet with Momir Nikolic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was your testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I assume the testimony today?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in reviewing your statement, did you notice anywhere in your statement where you indicated that you had been ordered by your commander, Mr. Borovcanin, to report to the Bratunac Brigade on the evening of the 16th to meet with Momir Nikolic. Is there anything in your statement about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no reference to that in my statement, but during my interview with the Office of the Prosecutor, I pointed out all these corrections to be made. I did say I remembered a number of additional details, and I did make it very clear after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So when you met with them to prepare for your examination here today a couple days ago, that's when you remembered that you had been ordered on the 16th by Mr. Borovcanin to meet with Momir Nikolic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it's your understanding that on the following day you attended a meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And during that meeting the issue of searching a particular area of the terrain was discussed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the area was divided as to who would search which area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated yesterday that during this meeting that -- it's somewhat unclear, that whether you actually met with the commander of the Bratunac Brigade or whether it was with the staff of the Bratunac Brigade. Would you clarify that.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the staff of the Bratunac Brigade for that meeting. I said I could not quite remember whether the commander was actually in attendance at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, of course, yesterday you indicated that you did not know Mr. Blagojevic at the time?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you say you didn't know, is that -- do you mean that you did not have the opportunity to be introduced to him or you didn't know what he even looked like?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I even knew what he looked like back then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that even during that staff meeting or the meeting that was held for the staff of the Bratunac Brigade on the morning of the 17th, you still did not know what Mr. Blagojevic looked like?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just said that I didn't know what he looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it, based on your testimony today and your memory, such that it is, that you have no recollection of actually meeting and speaking with the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I attended the meeting at the Bratunac Brigade, where an agreement was to be reached to search the terrain. And I said I didn't remember whether the commander of the Bratunac Brigade actually attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You indicate that there is this meeting. I take it you have some notes or something to reflect that a meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what if I were to tell you that Momir Nikolic, who seemed to be an awfully cooperative witness for the Prosecution, never mentioned anything about meeting you on the evening of the 16th in order for you to attend a meeting on the 17th. What would you say about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm only telling you what I was ordered to do and what I was supposed to carry out. I can't comment on anyone else's statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And, of course, you indicated yesterday that you did not know whether Momir Nikolic attended the meeting. Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the meeting was held. I know that certain activities were agreed as well as the deployment of forces, including the start line for this search. As to who attended the meeting, I've already said I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you knew Momir Nikolic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And assuming that there was a meeting and assuming that you attended this meeting, you would have seen Momir Nikolic, had he been there. Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Draw whatever conclusion you like. I told you, I don't remember who was at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you were asked a question: "Was Momir Nikolic there?" And I'm quoting from page 57, line 9, from yesterday's testimony of the transcript of yesterday. And your answer was: "I don't know." You did not state that you don't remember. You said that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now I'm telling you, I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you want to correct your answer from yesterday. Is that correct? You want to correct your answer from yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And then you were asked: "Who was in command of this operation?" And you indicated that it was a Captain Gavric. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Gavric was in command of the military and I was in command of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So there were two commanders there, as far as you understand, with respect to this searching operation?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several commanders, but Captain Gavric was the coordinator for both groups and so was I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So now he's not just a commander, but also he's a coordinator.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We coordinated the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, coordination is rather different from resubordination, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Coordination is something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So when you say that you were coordinating with Captain Gavric, you are not suggesting, sir, are you, that you were subordinated or resubordinated to the Bratunac Brigade and you are under the command of Captain Gavric, are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, I wasn't asking you where you were located at that time. We all know that. Do you remember my question?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You indicated that you were coordinating this activity, this searching activity, with Captain Gavric. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, coordination, we've already established, is different than resubordination, right? There's no sense in looking at the Prosecutor, just answer the question.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not looking at the Prosecutor. We sent a report concerning events on the ground to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters. And if you judge by that, this might imply that we were resubordinated to the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not asking you what it implies. I'm asking you to answer my questions. Now, you indicated that you were there commanding your men and coordinating with Captain Gavric. Is that your testimony, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, coordinating with Captain Gavric and I was at the meeting of the command of the Bratunac Brigade, and it was there that I received my order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you indicated that coordination is different from resubordination. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were not under the command of Captain Gavric while you were searching the terrain there, were you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were searching the ground and the command was located at the Bratunac Brigade staff headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were not under the command of Captain Gavric, were you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you were not resubordinated and under the command of Captain Gavric of the Bratunac Brigade, were you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, that is a multi-part question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, your microphone is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a multi-part question. It's an important question, but we're not sure which part the answer will be to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll break it down, Your Honour. I'll break it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were not resubordinated to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received my assignment at the Bratunac Brigade. That means that I was resubordinated to the Bratunac Brigade. The search was coordinated my Captain Gavric on behalf of the military and by myself on behalf of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So, Captain Gavric was able to direct you and your men as far as what you should do? He could give you orders?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Gavric commanded men on the ground, just like I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Stalin --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Stalin, did he give you orders?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, I don't know if he gave me orders, but certainly he had to give orders to his men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking if he gave orders to Stalin and if he gave orders to Stalin's men, and you're Stalin. Did he give you orders, Stalin, yes or no, and you would know that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received our orders from the command of the Bratunac Brigade, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's look and see what Mr. Gavric had told the Prosecutor when he was interviewed by the Office of the Prosecution on 28 November, 2001. And now I'm referring to what has been premarked for identification as D18/3. Incidentally, Mr. Jevic, are you -- do you enjoy the status of suspect as we speak right now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it's not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will get to that later, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I be allowed to answer this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Witness, the counsel has promised that we will come back to this question. Maybe you can answer that question when he comes back and not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could look at page 24, lines 3 through 6, and in the local version, in the B/C/S version, I don't seem to have it. According to

utterances.speaker: MR. GAVRIC HE SAYS
utterances.text: "I was there on behalf of the command of the Bratunac Brigade to link up and prevent any stupidities done in the field. The commander knew that I had a large influence on a lot of soldiers and officers." Now, Mr. Gavric says that he's there to link up. This is on page 24, lines 3 to 6. Now, if we could go through page 29, and I believe it's on page 25 of your version, the Srpski version. Line 5: Question: "Okay. Were you in command of this group of men?" This is a question being posed to Gavric. "I was not in command of that group, if you understand. I came on behalf of the command of the brigade just to link them up, link up the police and Zekic because they didn't know each other personally." Question: "Was Zekic remaining behind, were you in command?" Gavric: "No, all three of us went down in the field. We were in radio communication. We all went down towards the road." Now, if you go further down on the same page, line 19: "When you met up with these units and when you were there to link them up, did you pass on them what your commander had told you?"
